authoring.basis: Pinned source and test declarations only; no EduKids dependencies or application code were executed.

labelTaxonomy.POSITIVE: Pinned source directly supports the stated behavior or relationship.
labelTaxonomy.NEGATIVE: Pinned source contradicts the stated claim or establishes an absent behavior.
labelTaxonomy.MOCK_BOUND: The test declaration supports only the behavior of mocked boundaries or the shown mock setup.
labelTaxonomy.UNRESOLVED: Static evidence leaves a material path, state, or runtime property undecided.
labelTaxonomy.UNSUPPORTED: The available source and tests do not support the proposed conclusion.

labels.claim: AuthService.register checks for an existing email and raises ConflictException before hashing or creating a user.

expectedRelationship.testTitle: throws ConflictException when email already exists

allowedConclusions: The method checks an existing email before password hashing and user creation.
The test supplies an existing user and expects ConflictException.
prohibitedOverclaims: The test asserts user.create was not called.
The test verifies database uniqueness or concurrent registration.
labels.uncertainty: The test mocks persistence and only asserts the exception plus absence of refresh-session creation.

labels.claim: The successful registration unit test proves the service returns the mocked token values and requests a refresh session.

expectedRelationship.testTitle: registers successfully and returns auth payload

allowedConclusions: The test calls register, receives the mock token strings, and asserts createRefreshSession receives the refresh token.
prohibitedOverclaims: The test creates a signed JWT.
The test verifies a persisted user or refresh session.
labels.uncertainty: Prisma and AuthTokenService are mocks; only the method invocation and assertions are established.

labels.claim: Registration maps Prisma P2002 and PostgreSQL 23505 errors to ConflictException.
allowedConclusions: The catch block maps these two error codes to an email-conflict response.
prohibitedOverclaims: A test exercises this race-error mapping.
All database error codes are mapped to conflicts.
labels.uncertainty: No source test in this packet injects either persistence error code.

labels.claim: Login records a failed attempt and returns the same UnauthorizedException message for a missing user and a password mismatch.
allowedConclusions: Both branches record a failed attempt and throw UnauthorizedException with the same message.
prohibitedOverclaims: The behavior was exercised against Redis or a database.
The packet establishes rate-limit thresholds.
labels.uncertainty: This is a static source claim; no login service test was found in the supplied spec.

labels.claim: The production password hash call uses ten bcrypt salt rounds.
allowedConclusions: The comment says 10 while the actual bcrypt.hash call passes 12.
prohibitedOverclaims: The running production configuration has been inspected.
The discrepancy proves a security vulnerability.
labels.uncertainty: The static source contains an internal comment/code mismatch; runtime configuration was not checked.

labels.claim: The AuthController.login unit test proves the controller forwards its DTO to AuthService.login and returns the mock result.
allowedConclusions: The unit test calls the controller method and verifies the mocked service receives the DTO.
prohibitedOverclaims: The test verifies password comparison, rate limiting, persistence, or real token signing.
labels.uncertainty: AuthService is replaced by a Jest mock in the controller test module.

labels.claim: The supplied AuthService unit tests exercise AuthService.login for missing users and invalid passwords.
allowedConclusions: The supplied file contains registration tests and a switchProfile delegation test, not a login service test.
prohibitedOverclaims: No login tests exist anywhere in the repository.
The production login behavior is incorrect.
labels.uncertainty: This label is scoped to the pinned test file inspected for this pilot.

labels.claim: The successful registration test proves a cryptographically signed JWT is returned.

expectedRelationship.testTitle: registers successfully and returns auth payload

allowedConclusions: The test substitutes AuthTokenService and returns fixed strings.
prohibitedOverclaims: The strings are JWTs or were verified by a signing key.
labels.uncertainty: The real AuthTokenService and JWT library are outside this test boundary.

labels.claim: submitAnswer checks session ownership and current-question order before acquiring the in-flight lock.
allowedConclusions: Ownership and order guards precede lock acquisition in the shown method.
prohibitedOverclaims: These checks provide distributed locking.
The guards have been verified against a running cache.
labels.uncertainty: This order is read statically; runtime behavior depends on the session implementation and callers.

labels.claim: The in-flight answer test rejects when acquireAnswerLock returns false and does not release a lock it did not acquire.

expectedRelationship.testTitle: rejects submit when the same question is already in-flight

allowedConclusions: The mock returns false; the method rejects with BadRequestException; releaseAnswerLock is not called.
prohibitedOverclaims: The test exercises concurrent cache requests or successful answer submission.
labels.uncertainty: The test substitutes QuizSessionService and checks only the lock-rejection path.

labels.claim: The existingAnswer branch guarantees a client retry after a successful answer receives the prior result.
allowedConclusions: The method checks current order before existingAnswer; a successful answer increments currentQuestionIndex; the existing-answer return path is present.
prohibitedOverclaims: Sequential retries definitely succeed.
The branch is definitely unreachable under every runtime state.
labels.uncertainty: No test covers duplicate submission after a successful persisted session update; independent source and runtime review is required.

labels.claim: The supplied QuizService unit tests prove successful answer scoring, progress persistence, and event publication.
allowedConclusions: The shown tests cover a missing topic and an in-flight rejection path.
prohibitedOverclaims: No other repository test covers these behaviors.
The production side effects fail at runtime.
labels.uncertainty: The conclusion is limited to this pinned spec file and its visible test declarations.

labels.claim: The in-flight answer lock prevents duplicate processing across worker processes.
allowedConclusions: The shown lock key is stored in an instance field-backed Set.
prohibitedOverclaims: No database or cache-level duplicate protection exists elsewhere.
A cross-process duplicate was observed.
labels.uncertainty: Only this service implementation was inspected; deployment topology and persistence constraints require separate review.

labels.claim: submitAnswer updates the cached session and publishes a quiz-submitted event; database attempt/progress writes occur only for vocabulary-backed questions.
allowedConclusions: The shown branch guards repository attempt/progress writes with currentQuestion.vocabularyId, then saves the session and publishes an event.
prohibitedOverclaims: All quiz questions persist attempts in the same database tables.
Event delivery and cache persistence are transactionally atomic.
labels.uncertainty: No integration execution or transaction boundary is established by this source excerpt.

labels.claim: assertCurrentQuestionOrder accepts only questionId equal to currentQuestionIndex plus one.
allowedConclusions: A mismatched ID throws BadRequestException with the current-question message.
prohibitedOverclaims: All legitimate question IDs begin at one in every session.
labels.uncertainty: The method’s expected ID is derived from currentQuestionIndex; initialization is outside this location.

labels.claim: When Azure is configured and its provider returns an assessment, the service returns that result without calling the custom provider.

expectedRelationship.testTitle: uses Azure provider when configured and available

allowedConclusions: The test supplies an Azure result from a mock and asserts custom assessment is not called.
prohibitedOverclaims: The test calls Azure Speech or verifies cloud credentials and scoring.
labels.uncertainty: Both providers and configuration registry are mocked in this unit test.

labels.claim: If Azure is configured but returns no assessment, the service falls back to the custom provider.

expectedRelationship.testTitle: does not save a fabricated score when Azure is unavailable

allowedConclusions: The Azure branch throws ServiceUnavailableException when the result is null; the test asserts the custom provider is not called.
prohibitedOverclaims: Every pronunciation provider outage has identical HTTP behavior.
labels.uncertainty: The test uses a mocked null response; it does not simulate a real provider outage.

labels.claim: The custom provider path requires explicit CUSTOM configuration and an assessment input consisting of confidence or recognized text.

expectedRelationship.testTitle: uses custom assessment only when it is explicitly configured

allowedConclusions: The custom path is selected only after provider resolution and checks for confidenceScore or non-empty recognizedText.
prohibitedOverclaims: Audio alone is sufficient for a custom score.
labels.uncertainty: The provider result is a test fixture, not an independently calibrated score.

labels.claim: An audio-only custom assessment request without recognition text or confidence is rejected before calling the custom provider.

expectedRelationship.testTitle: rejects custom scoring when an audio-only request has no recognition result

allowedConclusions: The test asserts ServiceUnavailableException and that customProvider.assess was not called.
prohibitedOverclaims: All unsupported input combinations are rejected correctly.
labels.uncertainty: The test covers one audio-only input shape.

labels.claim: When assessment fails, the pronunciation service test asserts no quota cache write, attempt creation, or progress update.

expectedRelationship.testTitle: does not consume quota or save progress when provider assessment fails

allowedConclusions: The assessment mock rejects and the test checks cacheManager.set, repository.create, and updatePronunciationProgress were not called.
prohibitedOverclaims: The test exercises a real speech provider or a database transaction.
labels.uncertainty: Repository, assessment, and cache boundaries are mocked.

labels.claim: The custom provider's null-result fallback communicates a real zero pronunciation score and recognized transcript.
allowedConclusions: The fallback returns zero score fields, passed=false, and uses recognizedText or referenceText in the response.
prohibitedOverclaims: A listener actually produced the fallback transcript.
The fallback is persisted by the service.
labels.uncertainty: No supplied test covers a null custom-provider result or the downstream interpretation of this fallback.

labels.claim: The supplied Azure provider unit test proves live Azure Speech integration works.
allowedConclusions: A mocked Azure provider returns a fixed DTO and the service selects it.
prohibitedOverclaims: Network, credentials, API response mapping, latency, or deployed Azure configuration were tested.
labels.uncertainty: The provider boundary is mocked and the EduKids application is intentionally not executed.
